https://www.fenlandcitizen.co.uk/news/to.text: Home News Article Top Fenland Citizen stories include man hospitalised overseas, opening of Fenland’s first luxury cat hotel, and rapist to be deported By Molly Nicholas - Molly.Nicholas@iliffepublishing.co.uk Published: 06:00, 20 July 2026 Our biggest stories have featured a man hospitalised overseas, the opening of Fenland’s first luxury cat hotel, and a rapist to be deported. Meanwhile, an arsonist was jailed. Here are the biggest stories from last week across Fenland… GoFundMe page set up to help March man Danny Hayes who is fighting for life in Spain Danny is currently fighting for his life in hospital A fundraising page has been set up to support the family of a man who is fighting for his life in a hospital overseas. Danny Hayes, from March, remains in a medically-induced coma in Spain, currently “fighting for his life”, but his loved ones face high costs. After receiving “hundreds and hundreds of messages from people asking how they can help”, the family decided to start a GoFundMe page, which launched on Wednesday and has so far raised more than £6,460 of the £10,000 target, which will help fund the recovery of Mr Hayes. Part of Weasenham Lane in Wisbech closed while Anglian Water makes burst water main top priority The road has been closed while repair works are undertaken. Picture: Molly Nicholas A water company behind a hosepipe ban affecting the whole of Fenland has announced it is making a major water leak its priority. On Monday, one person took to social media with a video showing water spouting out of Weasenham Lane in Wisbech – outside of Wilco Motor Spares – with water building up and lying across the road. This area has become a hot spot for burst water mains and sinkholes in the past, with many long repair works taking place. Longcroft Luxury Cat Hotel opens new venue in Upwell Deputy mayor Vivienne Spikings (centre) cut the ribbon, alongside founding director Abi Purser (centre left) and owner Nichola Hannigan (centre right) A luxury cat hotel is up and running, ready to welcome pets to experience its “five-star boarding experience”. Longcroft Luxury Cat Hotel Upwell celebrated its grand opening last Sunday, greeting guests to Fenland’s first-of-its-kind premises. Deputy mayor Vivienne Spikings officiated the ribbon-cutting ceremony alongside hotel owners and family team Nichola Hannigan, her husband Andrew and mother Elaine. They were joined by Longcroft Luxury Cat Hotel founder Abi Purser. Arsonist jailed for setting light to number of vehicles in Chatteris and Wisbech Rolandas Fedoren has now been jailed. Picture: Cambs Police A man who set fire to numerous cars across Fenland has been jailed for more than a year. Rolandas Fedorenko, 25, torched a Nissan Juke in Furrowfields car park, Chatteris, in the early hours of April 1 last year. He lit a toilet roll and plastic and put it under the bumper, leaving the vehicle to burn out and damaging a nearby van and fence in the process. Then, later in the year, he began starting fires again. Former Wisbech mayor and rapist Aigars Balsevic to be deported when released from prison Aigars Balsevics, the former mayor of Wisbech, was convicted of rape in 2023 A former mayor who is serving time for rape has lost his legal battle to avoid deportation. Aigars Balsevics, 45, who made history as a town’s first mayor from Eastern Europe after taking on the role in Wisbech in 2020, has had his human rights appeal rejected by an Upper Tribunal judge following a long legal challenge. The Latvian national, who is serving a six-and-a-half-year sentence after being convicted of two counts of rape at Peterborough Crown Court in 2023, had argued deportation would affect his relationship with his two children – a son and daughter born in 2015 and 2017. Wisbech mum launches own Slimming World group after amazing weight loss Rosie after she lost four stone A woman who transformed her health, confidence and lifestyle with a weight loss group is now preparing to help others do the same. Rosie Harpum, a mum of one, knows first-hand how difficult managing weight can be while balancing the demands of family life. Having previously been a Slimming World member before becoming pregnant with her daughter, Rosie had enjoyed success with her weight loss journey. However, like many parents, her focus naturally shifted to caring for her family, and her own health gradually took a back seat. Human Interest Molly Nicholas MOST READ

http://www.bignewsnetwork.com/news/27926.text: Big News Network.com Polish farmers find cheer in harvest despite tough growing season by Yue Yuanyuan, Guo Shuang WARSAW, Aug. 24 (Xinhua) -- Folk music filled the air as people in traditional costumes danced, local residents sold agricultural products and handicrafts, and families wandered among stalls at a harvest festival in Warsaw over the weekend. The festival is one of Poland's long-standing rural traditions, held after the main fieldwork and harvests are completed. Traditionally, farmers give thanks for the crops they have gathered and celebrate the end of months of work in the fields. Yet behind this year's festive atmosphere lies a difficult growing season marked by sharp weather swings. Poland experienced unfavorable weather conditions for agriculture this year, according to Statistics Poland. In its preliminary estimate released in late July, the agency put production of basic cereals and cereal mixtures at 25.3 million tonnes this year, down about 4.9 percent from 2025. Rapeseed production was projected to fall 14.4 percent, while fruit harvested from trees was expected to decline by 18.6 percent and output from fruit bushes and berry plantations by 6.5 percent. The Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development has said frosts in April caused temperatures near the ground to fall as low as minus 10 degrees Celsius in some areas, damaging sour and sweet cherries, raspberries and currants. Drought added another layer of pressure. Poland's agricultural drought monitoring system found drought conditions affecting a wide range of crops between March and July, including cereals, rapeseed, fruit bushes and maize. Stanislaw and Barbara Wojcik, an elderly farming couple who grow wheat and rye and sell homemade bread at the festival, said "We harvested less wheat and rye than last year. There was too little rain at some stages, and the heat also affected the crops." The picture emerging from the harvest festival, however, was not entirely bleak. Alexander Sobolev, who sells bottled freshly pressed fruit juice and has lived in Poland for four years, said "apples are expected to be very good, and there were a lot of strawberries." For beekeeper Krzysztof Tomkielski, the changing weather brought more gains than losses. Sunny weather was particularly favorable for buckwheat honey. "There was more honey than last year," he said. The sector's resilience is also supported by government measures. Poland has 2.4 million bee colonies, the second-largest number in the European Union after Spain, and nearly 100,000 active beekeepers, according to the Polish government. Funding for this year's beekeeping support programs has been increased by 20 million zlotys (about 5.4 million U.S. dollars). The harvest may have been uneven, but the difficulties of the growing season did little to dampen the festive spirit. Music played, children watched folk performances, and farmers stood behind their stalls smiling and talking with visitors. "It is not only about having a very good harvest," said Sobolev. "People come here to be thankful for what they have and celebrate the work of the whole season." Photograph: Guy Smallman/Getty Images Holborn and St Pancras byelection Greens select Zack Polanski to run in Holborn and St Pancras byelection Leader has said Greens are underdogs in race for Keir Starmer’s former seat but he is confident they can beat Labour Helena Horton Fri 11 Sep 2026 06.18 EDT First published on Fri 11 Sep 2026 05.52 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Zack Polanski, the Green party leader, has been selected as its candidate for the Holborn and St Pancras byelection on 8 October. The seat became vacant this month when the former prime minister Keir Starmer announced he was leaving parliament . Polanski has said the Greens, which made gains in the area in the local elections in May, are underdogs in the race but he is confident they can beat Labour, which won the seat with a majority of more than 11,000 at the 2024 general election. On Wednesday, Labour selected the Camden council leader, Sagal Abdi-Wali, as its candidate. She said: “This place welcomed my family as refugees and gave us hope when we needed it most. I am so grateful to have had the opportunity to build a life here, serving our community as a councillor, school governor and community activist.” Some in Labour are understood to be concerned about the impact of upcoming oil and gas announcements on the campaign. Industry insiders expect the government to greenlight the Jackdaw gasfield as soon as next week, but there are expectations that any announcement on Rosebank, a contentious oilfield, will be delayed until after the byelection. Polanski won the race to stand for the Greens over one of the party’s local councillors, Hamza Chowdhury , who had said the constituency did not need “another MP who arrives during an election campaign” and “disappears once the votes are counted”. At a meeting to announce his candidacy, Polanski said: “The Greens might be the underdog in this election, but we have the momentum, and we can win. “And it’s clear everyone knows it’s the Green party against Labour, and before May we had one councillor here, and now we have 10. And last weekend we had so many people on the streets that we delivered leaflets to the entire constituency in just a few hours.” Announcing him as the candidate, Hannah Spencer, the MP for Gorton and Denton, acknowledged that the Labour party has the advantage. She said, “the next few weeks will be tough, of course. Labour have donations from fossil fuel lobbyists and gambling industries, and they have a big machine. But we are powered by people who care, and we have shown that we can beat the establishment parties, the billionaires, and I am living proof of that.” skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to First Edition Our morning email breaks down the key stories of the day, telling you what’s happening and why it matters after newsletter promotion Polanski said he lived in the constituency when he moved to London 20 years ago and that his barber is still there.
